questions.q: Which one of the following is a work attributed to playwright Bhasa?
questions.explain:
Bhasa was the first known Sanskrit dramatist, and many of his complete plays have been discovered. He wrote 5 plays based on Mahabharata episodes like Madhyamavyayoga, Pancharatra, Duta Vakyam, Duta Ghatotkacham, Karnabharam, Urubhangam.

Bhamaha was a scholar presumably of the 7th Century who dealt with Sanskrit poetics. He is believed to have composed the Sanskrit Kavyalankara and was a contemporary of Dandin.

The rules regarding performance, acting, gestures, stage direction and acting have been illustrated in the Natyashastra by Bharata.

Mahabhashya was written by Patanjali (2nd Century BCE). It is a commentary on selected rules of Sanskrit grammar from Paini's treatise, the Ashtadhyayi and Katyayana's Varttika.

questions.q:
With reference to Indian history, consider the following texts :
1. Nettipakarana
2. Parishishtaparvan
3. Avadanashataka
4. Trishashtilakshana Mahapurana
Which of the above are Jaina texts ?
questions.explain:
Nettipakarana is a Buddhist scripture.
Parishishtaparvan is a Jain text by Hemachandra.
Avadanashataka is a Buddhist text.
Trishashtilakshana Mahapurana is a famous Jain scripture.
Therefore, only 2 and 4 are Jaina texts.

questions.q: With reference to the history of ancient India, Bhavabhuti, Hastimalla and Kashemeshvara were famous
questions.explain:
Bhavabhuti was an Indian dramatist, playwright and poet known for his Sanskrit dramas.
Hastimalla was a poet and writer in the Hoysala Empire during the 13th century.
Kshemendra was a Kashmiri poet of Sanskrit who lived in the 11th century.
Thus, they were famous playwrights.

questions.q: Which one of the following books of ancient India has the love story of the son of the founder of Sunga dynasty?
questions.explain: The Malavikagnimitra is a Sanskrit play by Kalidas. It depicts the love story of Agnimitra, son of Pushyamitra (founder of the Sunga dynasty), who falls in love with the picture of an exiled servant girl named Malavika.

questions.q: The national motto of India, 'Satyameva Jayate' inscribed below the Emblem of India is taken from
questions.explain: Satyamev Jayate is the national motto of India. The words Satyameva Jayate are taken from Mundaka Upanishad, meaning 'Truth Alone Triumphs'.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. 'Bijak' is a composition of the teachings of Saint Dadu Dayal.
2. The Philosophy of PushtiMarg was propounded by Madhavacharya.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 1 is incorrect: Bijak is the best known of the compilations of Kabir, not Saint Dadu Dayal.\nStatement 2 is incorrect: The Philosophy of PushtiMarg was propounded by Vallabha (Vallabhacharya), not Madhavacharya.\nTherefore, neither statement is correct.
